size/explode: Backprop through time can make a gradient explode. This one has grown ten times over, to six, eight, and a step along it would throw the weights far off course.
size/norm: Clipping caps how big a gradient may get. Its size is its norm: the length of its arrow.
size/pyth: By Pythagoras, that is the square root of six squared plus eight squared: the square root of a hundred, which is ten.
size/dot: And six squared plus eight squared is just g dotted with itself. So the norm is the square root of g dot g, however many entries g has.
clip/threshold: Pick a threshold, c, here five. A gradient whose norm is at most c is left alone.
clip/scale: This norm is ten, over c, so multiply all of g by c over the norm: five over ten, one half. Six, eight becomes three, four.
clip/same: Both entries shrink by the same factor, so the arrow keeps its direction, and its new norm is exactly c.
clip/each: It is tempting to clip each entry on its own instead, to between minus c and c. Six, eight would become five, five.
clip/turns: But five, five is not a multiple of six, eight: eight was cut more than six, so that arrow points somewhere else. Scaling cuts every entry by the same factor, so it never turns the step.
step/step: Then take the gradient step as usual, with the clipped gradient. From w at one, two, with step size zero point one, the step is zero point three, zero point four, and w lands at zero point seven, one point six.
step/raw: Unclipped, the step would have been twice as long. However far a gradient explodes, a clipped step never goes further than eta times c.
